clue.text: Drunk eating cold stew

indicators.note: something eating takes another thing inside it, so the first word swallows the second

blocks.note: a souse is an old word for a drunkard
C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap

explanation.surface: A tipsy diner is tucking into a cold bowl of stew.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUSE takes C inside to make SCOUSE, a meat and vegetable stew from Liverpool, which also gives Liverpudlians their nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Scouse is a specific regional dish, a Liverpool lamb or beef hotpot, so it is an example of a stew.

clue.text: Clutch extremely, well, close to brake and throttle

indicators.note: extremely points at the extremities of the word, its two outermost letters
the close of a word is its final letter, so only its ending is kept

blocks.note: first and last letters of clutch
well in the sense of all right, fine
last letter of brake

explanation.surface: Motoring instructions: work the clutch, brake and throttle properly.
explanation.walkthrough: Clutch, brake and throttle all look like car controls; a choke is one too, but here throttle is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To choke someone is to strangle them by squeezing the neck, the same violent act as throttling.

clue.text: Unqualified dunce essentially interrupting expert's statement

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its very centre, so only the middle letter is wanted
to interrupt is to break into something, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: unqualified as in complete, absolute
an ace is an expert
middle letter of dunce

explanation.surface: A real fool butts in while a specialist is making a formal statement.
explanation.walkthrough: Unqualified suggests lacking credentials, which suits the dunce, but here it means total, absolute; the 's of expert's merely links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An utterance is anything spoken aloud, a remark or declaration, so it can serve as a statement.

clue.text: Reveal stance in support of electronic vote

indicators.note: in a down entry a support sits underneath, so this part comes after the others

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
a cross on a ballot paper marks a vote
a pose is a stance or posture

explanation.surface: A politician reveals where they stand on electronic voting.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose something is to uncover it and lay it open to view, which is what revealing means.

clue.text: Saves defender getting on end of crosses

indicators.note: getting on the end of something means attaching at its tail, so this word is placed last

blocks.note: crosses as in goes across, cuts across
a back is a defensive player in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A football report: a defender meets the crosses and saves the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Saves, defender and crosses all suggest a match; saves is really about economising.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cuts back reduces their spending, which is a way of economising or putting money aside.

clue.text: Crazy dreams of rooks flying?

blocks.note: the rook in chess is also called the castle
anything flying is aloft, off the ground

explanation.surface: Someone imagines crows taking off in a crazy reverie.
explanation.walkthrough: Rooks look like the birds, which fits flying, but they are chess pieces; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Castles in the air is an idiom for impractical schemes and daydreams that have no foundation in reality.

clue.text: Stage actor ultimately missing out on a lead in Mexican TV show

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the last letter is taken
a word missing out on something goes without it, so that letter is dropped
the lead of a word is its front, its opening letter

blocks.note: the stage as a profession or place of drama
last letter of actor, the one removed
taken as written
first letter of Mexican

explanation.surface: A performer misses out on a starring role in a Mexican television series.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a Mexican telenovela, but the show is the 1980s American action series; the hyphen in A-Team splits its letters oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: The A-Team was a popular American action television series about a band of fugitive ex-soldiers turned mercenaries.

clue.text: Nurse with answer following thumbnail picture

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the earlier pieces are placed behind the later word

blocks.note: a thumbnail sketch is short and concise
EN is an Enrolled Nurse
to counter is to answer back

explanation.surface: A nurse and a reply turn up beside a little thumbnail image.
explanation.walkthrough: Picture here means a film: Brief Encounter is the 1945 David Lean romance set in a railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: Picture is an old word for a movie, and Brief Encounter is a classic British film.

clue.text: Screen Dundee clubs put on right before Old Firm Derby is large enough initially

definitions.note: the answer completes the film title Crocodile Dundee

indicators.note: in a down entry, something put on another sits above it
before means placed ahead of what follows
initially points at the opening letters of each of the preceding words

blocks.note: C is clubs, the card suit
R is the abbreviation for right
O is the abbreviation for old
Co is company, a firm
first letters of Derby, is, large and enough

explanation.surface: Football in Scotland: Dundee, the Old Firm derby between Celtic and Rangers, and whether a crowd is big enough.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Firm is the Glasgow rivalry of Celtic and Rangers; here Old and Firm split into O and CO. The definition is the film's title missing its first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocodile Dundee is the 1986 Australian comedy film, so the screen Dundee is named by this word.

clue.text: Sauce brand also liking bottles – it normally comes in tubes

indicators.note: a word that bottles something holds it inside like a container

blocks.note: too means also
a taste for something is a liking for it
HP is a well-known British brown sauce

explanation.surface: A brand of sauce, also bottled, praised for its taste.
explanation.walkthrough: HP is a well-known British brown sauce. Bottles looks like containers for sauce but is the verb for holding inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothpaste is a cleaning paste sold squeezed from flexible tubes, so the cryptic description fits it.

clue.text: Press club

blocks.note: first meaning: smooth clothes with a heated appliance
second meaning: a golf club with an angled metal head

explanation.walkthrough: Press club sounds like a journalists' society; the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for flattening creases from clothing and a noun for a type of golf club.

clue.text: 18 Across regularly taking trains – badly needing compensation

indicators.note: taking means picking up and adding on the following letters
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: 18 Across is a salesman, shortened to rep
second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters of trains badly

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman, badly let down by the trains, wants his money back.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash splits trains from badly in the surface, but the alternate letters run straight across both words.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal was originally the seizure of goods as redress for an injury, so it once meant compensation obtained by force.

clue.text: Finally caught the criminal exporting drug – it won't stick

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so the last letter of each following word is taken
something exported is sent out, so it leaves the word

blocks.note: last letters of caught and the
a felon is a criminal
E is ecstasy, the drug, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A criminal smuggling drugs is finally caught but nothing sticks to him.
explanation.walkthrough: Finally covers both caught and the. A Teflon politician is one whom scandal never sticks to, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Teflon is the trademarked non-stick coating used on frying pans, valued because food does not adhere to it.

clue.text: Last and first of patients in hospital

indicators.note: first of means the opening letter of the next word
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a san is a sanatorium, a kind of hospital
first letter of patients

explanation.surface: A patient's final days and first days in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Last and first look like a pair of positional instructions; last is actually the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To span a period is to extend across it, and to last is to continue through time, so the verbs overlap.

clue.text: New Mac not opening clipart for real

indicators.note: not opening means without its opening, so the first letter goes
new letters make something fresh, so the fodder is rearranged into a new word

blocks.note: Mac without its first letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A new Apple Mac computer won't open a clip-art file.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mac is an Apple computer, and clipart is ready-made images, so the surface is about a software glitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical can describe something actual or in effect rather than theoretical, close to the sense of real.

clue.text: All season, Mike's working with a new deceptive pitcher

indicators.note: letters set working are put into action and moved about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A baseball pitcher named Mike plays all season with a new deceptive delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitcher looks like baseball but means a salesman making a sales pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake-oil salesman peddles fake remedies with a smooth sales pitch, a fraud who deceives buyers.

clue.text: See 7
Open in the morning – with permit

indicators.note: with means accompanied by, so one part simply joins the other

blocks.note: am is ante meridiem, before noon
to enable is to permit or allow

explanation.surface: A shop sign says open in the morning, with a licence.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amenable is receptive and willing to be persuaded, meaning open to suggestions.

clue.text: See 15
Scorsese oddly ignored Canadian people

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are ignored, so only the even ones remain

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of Scorsese

explanation.surface: Martin Scorsese strangely overlooked a Canadian people in his film.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cree are a First Nations people of Canada, one of the country's largest indigenous groups.

clue.text: Son joining book groups

indicators.note: joining means attached to, so one piece is added to the next

blocks.note: to book something is to order it in advance
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son joins book clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Orders are classes or ranks, such as religious orders or taxonomic orders, so they are kinds of groups.

clue.text: Soloist originally meant to play viola part?

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so only the first letter is used
to play with letters is to move them about into a new order

blocks.note: first letter of soloist
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A soloist was meant to play a viola part.
explanation.walkthrough: Viola looks like the instrument, but it is the flower, the pansy family; the question mark signals the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: The stamen is the pollen-producing organ of a flower, so it is part of a viola plant.

clue.text: Wine some doctor's imbibed

indicators.note: something imbibed is swallowed and held within the words

blocks.note: found inside some doctor's

explanation.surface: A doctor has knocked back some wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a red Bordeaux wine from the region of that name on the Gironde estuary in France.

clue.text: Powerhouse deciphered clues after the penny drops in just seconds

indicators.note: deciphering means working out a code, rearranging letters into sense
after means coming later, so this piece is placed behind the next
only the second letters of the following words are wanted

blocks.note: second letters of the, penny and drops
the letters of clues, rearranged

explanation.surface: A solver works out the clues quickly once the penny drops.
explanation.walkthrough: The penny drops is an idiom for sudden understanding, so it reads as the moment of solving; here it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercules, the mythical hero of great strength, is a byword for a strong and powerful person.

clue.text: Cream tea snubbed by priest

indicators.note: snubbed hints at stubbed or cut short, so its last letter is lopped
by means beside, so the pieces sit next to each other

blocks.note: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel
tea without its final letter

explanation.surface: A cream tea is snubbed by a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: Cream tea is a British treat of scones, jam and clotted cream; here the two words separate.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its best part, and the elite are the best of a group.

clue.text: LSD in bag discovered by police unit

indicators.note: discovered here means uncovered, with the covering outer letters stripped off
by means beside, so the pieces sit next to each other

blocks.note: bag with its first and last letters removed
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Police detectives discover LSD in a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid is the slang name for the hallucinogenic drug lysergic acid diethylamide, better known by its initials.

clue.text: Bento boxes feed computer department – just not first

indicators.note: a word that boxes another encloses it like a box

blocks.note: taken as written
to feed is to eat
IT is information technology, the computer department

explanation.surface: Bento boxes are delivered to feed the IT department, though they are not the first served.
explanation.walkthrough: A bento is a Japanese boxed lunch, so boxes looks like a noun; it is the verb enclosing EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: If someone beat you to it, they got there first, so you only narrowly failed to be first.

clue.text: Entirely audible safety signal

blocks.note: all means entirely, wholly
clear in the sense of easily heard

explanation.surface: A safety signal that can be heard everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The all-clear is the siren or sign given when danger has passed, telling people it is now safe.

clue.text: 80s band making comeback film – it's sweet

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the band's name is read the other way

blocks.note: Bros were a British boy band of the late 1980s
ET is the 1982 Spielberg film

explanation.surface: An 80s band makes a comeback film, which is a sweet thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Bros really did make a comeback documentary, After the Screaming Stops, which adds to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorbet is a frozen dessert of sugared fruit juice, so it is a sweet course.
